3291020.summary: Resolves a unit transforming out of a remnant: marks the target card as transforming and starts its transform animation with a callback. If no animation wait is needed it finishes the action here (reassemble minions, hero-death check, turn UI refresh).
comments: Closure captures a copy of the battle action and this manager for the transform callback.
Log which card is transforming.
Mark the card as a unit mid-transformation.
Start the remnant transform; the callback captured above runs when it completes.
Animation still pending: return now, the callback is expected to finish the action later.
No animation to wait for: finish the action immediately (same epilogue as other Resolve methods).
Action done and queue empty: if either side's minions are out of position, queue a reassemble order.
No automatic actions left in the queue: time to check whether the battle is over.
Tutorial and campaign matches skip the hero-death check here.
Reads each hero's card state; 5 seems to be waitingToDie, i.e. a hero is dead.
Battle already in PostBattle: warn and bail out unless a forced disconnect loss is pending.
Opponent disconnected and the local player should lose: record the result and run the normal end sequence.
Normal end: enter PostBattle, stop the battle loop and tell the other player the match finished.
In networked games the match-finished message is sent to the other player.
Player's hero survived (enemy hero died): raise an enemy health change signal with the enemy hero's health.
Work out the winner from which hero died.
Build the ranked match result from Elo rating and XP, then fill in skull milestones for both sides.
Match types 0x14, 0xd2 and 0xb4 (seem to be special event modes) notify LiveOps that a human won.
Store the result, then finish the battle (results screen and rewards).
Neither hero is dead: just broadcast the while-in-play effects and carry on.
Action resolution is over: clear the resolving flag so new actions can start.
Enemy's turn: re-enable the enemy minions and recompute whether the enemy hero can act or attack.
Hero can act only if it is the enemy's, in play, has attacks left (bloodthirst allows a second) and is not stunned.
Ferocity/Oath heroes: recompute canAct, and switch to Active attack type if still summon sick.
Show or hide the hero's attack-ready indicator on its card UI.
Player's turn: highlight playable cards and re-enable minions and the hero.
Nothing queued: start a garbage collection while idle and resume the turn clock.
If the player can act, count the available actions; with only end turn left (outside a tutorial restriction) show the no-actions UI.
Tutorial scripting: after a manual player action, resume scripted steps if they were waiting on it.
Reset the manual-action marker for the next sequence.
Shared failure label: a null manager or hero reference (compiler null checks).

3295b58.summary: Removes pending actions tied to a card that is leaving play (its self-buffs). Cancels its effects from the action, instant and interrupt queues, then scans the delayed instant queue backwards and cancels matching actions.
comments: Cancel the card's own queued effects from the three main queues.
Now scan the delayed instant queue; a null queue falls through to the null-reference throw.
Walk the queue from the end so removals do not shift unvisited entries.
Only actions that came from this card matter.
Action type 1 is skipped.
Action must also target this card (or have no card to compare against).
Certain action types (0x2d with sub-type 0x28, 0x1a, 0x2d) end the scan; decompiler may have lost a continue here.
Log and cancel the action from the queue.

3295ac4.summary: Hides the active ability description and restores the selected card's highlight: frames come back and the glow colors are tweened back. Called when an active ability display should stop, e.g. after targeting is done or cancelled.
comments: Only act if the active skill description panel exists.
Fade the ability description out.

Bring the card frames back and clear the display flag.
Reset the Energy cost icon's scale.
Kill any running color tween on the highlight before starting a new one.
No fade time: set the glow colors immediately.
Hide the glow object (decompiler output unreliable near the null checks).
Fade time set: build a tween sequence that fades the glow colors back.
Insert a callback into the sequence to finish the frame color change.
